// why weft

One file, two runtimes, no glue.

Most of a web app is the code that moves data between a server and a browser. Weft writes that code for you.

  • Server and client in the same file

    A server() function runs on the server, everywhere else runs in the browser - weft cuts the file in two and types the call between them.

    const add = server(async (text: string) => db.todos.insert({ text }));
     
    export default function Todos() {
      return <form action={add}><input name="text" /></form>;
    }
    split at build
  • 9.4 KBmin + br

    A runtime you can read

    The whole client runtime is 9.4 KB compressed - smaller than most hero images.

    See the numbers

  • Islands that stream

    Each interactive part ships and wakes up on its own, as its data arrives - the page never waits for the slowest.

  • Routes you can type

    The file tree is the router; links are checked by the compiler.

    • / routes/index.tsx
    • /todos routes/todos.tsx
    • /blog/:slug routes/blog/[slug].tsx

  • Zero config, all escape hatches

    Sensible defaults for TypeScript, CSS, images and env vars. A config file when you need one - and only the line you change.

  • Hot reload you do not notice

    Save a file and the change is on screen before you look up - state kept.

    38 ms

  • Runs where you deploy

    One build, many targets: Bun, Node, Deno, Cloudflare Workers or a folder of static files.

    All adapters

// try it

Read the code, then run it.

Three files make an app. The terminal is real - type into it.

import { server } from 'weft';
import { db } from '../server/db';
import Counter from '../islands/Counter';
export const load = server(() => db.posts.latest(5));
export default function Home({ data }) {
  return (
    <main>
      {data.map((p) => <a href={`/blog/${p.slug}`}>{p.title}</a>)}
      <Counter start={3} />
    </main>
  );
}
import { sqlite } from 'weft/db';
// never sent to the browser - weft refuses to bundle it
export const db = sqlite('app.db', {
  posts: { slug: 'text', title: 'text', at: 'date' },
});
import { signal } from 'weft';
// an island: 0.6 KB of JavaScript, awake when it scrolls into view
export default function Counter({ start }: { start: number }) {
  const n = signal(start);
  return <button onClick={() => n.value++}>{n}</button>;
}

// changelog

Four releases, nothing broke.

A minor release every quarter; an upgrade is one command and has needed no codemod since 4.0.

  1. 4.3 Partial prerendering

    A route's static shell comes from the CDN; its islands are filled in at the edge.

    December 2026 · in beta

  2. 4.2 Islands that stream

    • feature Islands wake in the order their data arrives - the page never waits for the slowest query.
    • feature Typed form actions: a form's fields are checked against the server function it posts to.
    • speed The dev server starts 40 % faster; the module graph is cached between runs.
    • fix Source maps point at the line you wrote, not at the split.
    4 November 2026 · latest

  3. 4.1 Routes you can type

    Links are checked by the compiler: a renamed file fails the build, not your users.

    12 August 2026

  4. 4.0 One thread

    server() functions live in the file that calls them; the API layer is gone.

    5 May 2026
0breaking changes

Upgrade in one line

The upgrade reads your lockfile, moves every weft package and runs the codemods a release needs.

bunx weft upgrade
weft build && weft deploy
